# ISSUE-46 implementation plan

Restore Relay 07's local SPOOL-02 from DEEP FIELD. A player can use either Q17 proof, learn the operation order in The Forgotten Archive, and then apply it at the Recovery Console. The saved restore fact unlocks the SPOOL-02 map sector, Maintenance Annex and MAINTAINER access.

## Dimensions

The approved size is `multi_area` and the execution profile is `detailed`. Estimate 4–8 hours for implementation and focused verification, with time for review and the existing browser workflow within the 32-hour claim budget. The chief implementation uncertainty is the entry bundle headroom.

## What we know

- Acts I–II already work from Episode 000 completion. DEEP FIELD requires `completed:episode.000`. Reading the Q17 index and running `SEARCH Q17` opens the desks. The header desk requires the departure ledger, headers and queue policy. The custody desk requires the originals, comparison and migration hold receipt. Each accepts `SUBMIT DEFERRED` and returns its own confirmation. The confirmation events grant `flag:deferred-headers-verified` or `flag:deferred-custody-verified` and both grant exactly `flag:deferred-verified`. See `content/bbs/deep-field.json:5`, `content/bbs/forgotten-board.json:9`, `content/bbs/q17-header-desk.json:9`, `content/bbs/q17-custody-desk.json:9`, `content/events/q17-header-confirmation.json:3` and `content/events/q17-custody-confirmation.json:3`.
- The Forgotten Archive opens on the shared proof fact. Its `shelf-order` puzzle requires inspecting `seal-fragment`, `route-fragment` and `ack-fragment`. The correct order sets the local `order-learned` flag, whose reward rule grants exactly `flag:spool-02-order-learned`. The door host saves its slot and earned rewards in one write. The training route already includes a readable notebook and EXIT to the signed-in menu. See `content/doors/forgotten-archive.json:10`, `:50`, `:287`, `:318`, `:323`, `src/doors/host.ts:83` and `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:988`.
- A BBS board check currently takes one token and reads a unique event-only response. The existing effect settles the message read, event grants and bulletin before writing the save. Subsequent uses redisplay the response without another write. The view applies the effect before reading screen actions, so a new flag can immediately affect BBS navigation. See `src/content/schema.ts:233`, `src/bbs/bbs.ts:338`, `src/bbs/bbs.ts:346`, `src/bbs/progress.ts:80`, `src/progress/events.ts:5` and `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:29`.
- The BBS directory currently exposes DOORS and NETWORK. NETWORK already lists visible sectors through `mapNodes`. The same map filter serves the hub. BBS menu and hub STATUS derive the highest eligible rank, and repeatable BBS dialogue uses the highest-priority applicable line. PACKET and GHOST profiles are already historical output without TALK. See `src/bbs/bbs.ts:222`, `:236`, `:483`, `:567`, `src/app/tools.ts:113`, `src/main.ts:94`, `src/world/map.ts:9`, `src/progress/access.ts:4` and `src/narrative/dialogue.ts:24`.
- The restoration row calls for a readable target card, transfer of shelf knowledge, and a single successful restoration with originals preserved. ECHO discusses source dependencies and SYSOP grants local maintenance permission. PACKET and GHOST appear through historical Annex annotations. The future doors and reconstruction depend on the shared `flag:spool-02-restored`. See `docs/game-design.md:118`, `:122`, `:126`, `:157`, `:165` and `:177`.
- Approved snapshot baseline in a writable copy using Node 24.22.3 and cached locked dependencies. `npm run content:validate` passed with 87 records, content version `b3a285bb`. The focused selection passed 179 tests across five files. Playwright collected 12 existing tests across the BBS and startup specs. The build and `gzipSync(readFileSync(path)).length / 1024` passed with `index-Cn4M9p2n.js` at 59,546 bytes (58.1504 KiB) and `environment-esavcwi0.js` at 132,330 bytes (129.2285 KiB). The index has 1,894 bytes of headroom. Logs are `install.log`, `content.log`, `focused.log`, `collection.log`, `build.log` and `gzip.log` under `../scratch/issue-46-base.IVChra/`. Git metadata is absent in the planner sandbox. The snapshot input checksum list `source.sha256` hashes to `ae8143ac11259941079142de81f0fe661716f1e0fe373c5bfa23ef47d5a62c4e`.

## What we're assuming

- A read-only Recovery Console target card can appear after the player has either prerequisite. Both facts are required to expose operation controls and apply an order. The knowledge-only state is a deliberately incomplete saved state for verifying the proof predicate. The live shelf itself requires proof. The first progression test checks all four gate combinations.
- The Annex can use a BBS message board reached from DIRECTORY, with a build recipe in the board description and three sealed source records in a thread. The SPOOL-02 map sector provides a read-only description of the local working spool. Steps 1 and 3 check that both affordances are usable through existing views.
- The normalized JSON and any shared schema changes can fit in the entry bundle. Measure after the first working checkpoint and on the final development candidate. Keep order dispatch in the lazy BBS connection path, and avoid serialized defaults on existing boards.

## Open questions

- The final compressed sizes depend on the candidate build. Step 4 measures both chunks with the Browser tests algorithm. Reduce in-scope additions if either budget is exceeded and reopen the plan if meeting the limit needs changes to startup, existing content or build structure.
- Keyboard focus, pointer operation and continued startup behavior need the production-browser path. The configured agent path is isolated native Codex on Linux (`.swarm/config.yaml:4`, `:16`, `:63`). The planner has no browser grant. The existing GitHub Actions job runs Chromium on Ubuntu via Playwright and serves `dist/` under `/signal-lost/` by request interception (`.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11`, `playwright.config.ts:5`, `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:18`). This is a static browser game with localStorage and no service backend. Other OS and harness combinations are outside the approved execution path.

## Implementation sequence

1. **Expose the Recovery Console in the signed-in BBS directory.** In `src/content/schema.ts` extend `bbsMessageBoardSchema` with optional `directory` and `orderCheck` fields. A directory board uses the existing BOARD and thread model. Keep the current token `check` contract and reject a board that declares both check modes. The new check declares the required facts and their missing-evidence text, the ordered operation tokens and out-of-order feedback, a prompt, invalid-order feedback and a response message ID. Validate distinct uppercase operation tokens and distinct required facts. In `src/bbs/bbs.ts`, reuse the shared board lookup and access check for `BOARD <id>` from DIRECTORY, filter listings by their current conditions, and route BACK from directory boards to DIRECTORY and from their threads to the originating board. Keep ordinary boards under BOARDS and keep DOORS and NETWORK in place. Author `content/bbs/spool-02-recovery.json` as a directory board with an any-of visibility requirement for the two exact facts. The target card identifies SPOOL-02 under Relay 07 and states “RESTORE WORKING SPOOL. RETAIN SEALED ORIGINALS.” The prompt asks for the training shelf procedure. Add a menu breadcrumb in `content/bbs/deep-field.json` gated on the learned fact, pointing to DIRECTORY / RECOVERY CONSOLE. Both the locked card and eligible prompt use plain terminal text.
2. **Apply one complete order and save one restore fact.** Extend `createBbs` in `src/bbs/bbs.ts` with board-local draft operations. Offer operation buttons alphabetically once eligible using `ORDER <operation>`. Disable selected operations and enable `CLEAR` when there is a draft. Report the staged sequence in text, and enable the bare APPLY button only for a full draft. Accept typed `APPLY <operation> / <operation> / <operation>` through the same check. Tolerate case and whitespace variation, reject incomplete orders, duplicates, unknown tokens and surplus arguments, and discard the draft when leaving the console. Recheck both facts at dispatch before interpreting the order. A blocked submission gives the relevant authored missing-evidence line and the menu exposes no operation actions while blocked. Wrong permutations report the failed operation's missing input, such as ACK's destination receipt, and point back to the notebook for retry. Neither drafting nor rejection returns an effect. Declare the three ordered-check verbs separately in `src/content/schema.ts` and include them in the validator's reserved secret-command set. Keep them out of the enum that keys the required BBS interface copy and out of the one-token check schema. Use the existing terminal dispatch and action buttons in `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts` and `src/terminal/terminal.ts`.

   Extract the response-handling tail of `checkAnswer` and share it with the ordered check. Add `content/bbs/spool-02-restoration-receipt.json` as an event-only DEEP FIELD message and `content/events/spool-02-restored.json` to grant `spool-02-restored` and post that receipt on its own `bbs-read:spool-02-restoration-receipt`. The successful check is the route that can first create that read. It writes the read, bulletin and restore fact together through the existing BBS effect and event settlement. Reapplying the right order returns the same receipt without another effect, save write, fact or bulletin. Keep the existing BBS in-tab behavior and save-refused feedback if storage rejects a write. In `src/content/validate.ts`, include the ordered check in unique response ownership and same-endpoint/own-read bulletin validation, resolve its prerequisite facts, and retain current Q17 evidence diagnostics. The actual event grant enters the existing flag producer index, which resolves all restore consumers.
3. **Make the restored state playable.** Add `content/sectors/spool-02.json` with the restore fact as its visibility gate, map coordinates near Relay 07 and readable local-spool information on entry. Add `content/access-levels/maintainer.json` at rank 2 gated directly by the restore fact. Add `content/bbs/maintenance-annex.json` with the same visibility gate, a directory link and the build recipe. Its `maintenance-annex-fragments` thread opens SC-1 `signature-checker`, QR-1 `queue-reader` and RW-1 `replay-writer` records with their complete local boundaries, seals, dependencies and retained annotations. The recipe orders SC-1, then QR-1, then RW-1. Author PACKET's routing and GHOST's provenance annotations as old records inside the fragment evidence. Add repeatable, priority-5 BBS lines gated by the restore fact to `content/characters/echo.json` and `content/characters/sysop.json`. ECHO identifies readable dependencies and SYSOP confirms MAINTAINER on a working copy with the original read-only. Keep both Q17 confirmations readable through MESSAGES. The restore fact is the prerequisite contract for #31 and #32. Door registrations, manifests, comparison/submission logic, replay and Chapter completion belong to their respective WorkUnits (#31, #32 and #37).
4. **Exercise the complete progression and measure bundle budgets.** Extend the existing unit and e2e specs named below. Run the focused commands and use the development gzip procedure in TEST_PLAN.md as soon as the feature builds and again on the final candidate if relevant inputs changed. Preserve the existing lazy BBS import, production content loading and environment loading paths. Keep the current episode, both Forgotten Archive browser journeys, FORGE, Observatory and budget coverage. Deliver the source identity and logs for tester review and CI traceability.

## HANDOFF

**Entry points and symbols**

- `src/content/schema.ts:233` (`bbsMessageBoardSchema`, new `orderCheck` field and ordered-check verbs) and `src/content/validate.ts:181`, `:306`, `:616`, `:726` (`checkBbsReferences`, producer and condition checks).
- `src/bbs/bbs.ts:134`, `:261`, `:272`, `:346`, `:394`, `:508` (`screen`, `showBoard`, `back`, `checkAnswer`/shared receipt, and `dispatch`). Use `getBbsOffer` at `src/bbs/offer.ts:31` to collect existing board records. Live integrations to exercise are `createBbsConnection` at `src/bbs/connection.ts:23`, `createBbsDoorSession` at `src/bbs/door-session.ts:9`, and `createBbsProgress` at `src/bbs/progress.ts:80`.
- `content/bbs/deep-field.json:16` (menu breadcrumb), `content/characters/echo.json:367` and `content/characters/sysop.json:45` (new BBS line after priority 4). Consumer seams are `mapNodes` at `src/world/map.ts:9`, `deriveAccessLevel` at `src/progress/access.ts:4`, and `createScriptedDialogue` at `src/narrative/dialogue.ts:24`.
- New content paths, each checked absent in the approved snapshot by exact path `content/bbs/spool-02-recovery.json`, `content/bbs/spool-02-restoration-receipt.json`, `content/bbs/maintenance-annex.json`, `content/bbs/maintenance-annex-fragments.json`, `content/bbs/annex-signature-checker.json`, `content/bbs/annex-queue-reader.json`, `content/bbs/annex-replay-writer.json`, `content/events/spool-02-restored.json`, `content/sectors/spool-02.json` and `content/access-levels/maintainer.json`.

**Existing tests and fixtures**

- Extend the two desk cases, shelf continuation and memory-save helpers in `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:644`, `:729`, `:773`, `:988`. Add focused producer, prerequisite, ownership and order authoring cases to `tests/unit/content.test.ts:1360`. Keep `tests/unit/access.test.ts:18`, `tests/unit/world.test.ts:35` and `tests/unit/voices.test.ts:13` as focused regression coverage.
- Extend `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` using its keyboard/pointer helpers at lines 14–45 and `seedSaveOnce` at `tests/e2e/helpers.ts:5`. Derive the eligible save in the test from `tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json` and the current `freshSave` shape. Extend `tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts:3` to check that startup still defers BBS and does not fetch content JSON or the manifest.
- Run `npm run content:validate`, `npm test -- tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/unit/access.test.ts tests/unit/world.test.ts tests/unit/voices.test.ts` and `npm run build`. Use the exact targeted format/lint, Playwright collection and Node gzip commands in TEST_PLAN.md. CI runs `npm run test:e2e`.

**Checked assumptions and reopen conditions**

- Verified both Q17 events, the Archive's three inspections and local-to-global reward rule, rehydration via the existing versioned save, and the environment and entry budgets. The legacy fixture sets FORGE already open, so explicitly remove `forge-opened` in the other branch. Running the focused tests on the base confirmed the existing Acts I–II and locked map behavior before planning the extension.
- Reopen if either exact prerequisite producer differs in the implementation base, the recovery interaction needs a save or startup change, either compressed limit requires broader work, or the restored content would require a future route or reconstruction. A browser failure in this feature should be reproduced in its CI path and addressed in the planned scope.

### What this change breaks

- `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:842` currently forbids every occurrence of SPOOL-02 after Q17. Narrow that assertion to prohibit the restored sector, Annex, MAINTAINER and restore fact before success. Test Recovery Console discovery separately. Keep the damaged directory's inaccessible source labels and the retained Q17 confirmations.
- `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:1097` checks the transfer from the Archive before any restoration. Keep its exact fact set at EXIT, then assert restoration effects only after the console accepts the order. Keep existing normal-board action and single-token diagnostics, including `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:1106` and `tests/unit/content.test.ts:1418`.
- Repository search located the affected story contract in `docs/game-design.md:146` and `:163`, the save/renderer contract in `docs/architecture.md:31`, and authored BBS access, events and dialogue rules in `docs/content-authoring.md:80`, `:104`, `:118`. Preserve these and the existing issue templates. The new files implement the story facts as documented.
- Preserve the assertions in `tests/e2e/journey.spec.ts:4`, `tests/e2e/map.spec.ts:4`, `tests/e2e/forge.spec.ts:4`, `tests/e2e/progress.spec.ts:95`, the Q17/Archive journeys in `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:229` and `:301`, and the budgets in `tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts:13`. Keep `src/main.ts:58` and `:143` on their current loading paths and use the existing Browser tests workflow.

# ISSUE-46 test plan

Numbering follows the four acceptance criteria in `WORKUNIT.md:26`–`:29`. The approved base smoke checks and gzip measurements are recorded in PLAN.md. Candidate checks use the shipped content and the same runtime paths as the player.

## Acceptance coverage

### 1. Either Q17 proof plus the real training shelf

Parameterize the `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:644` journey over header and custody, each with FORGE opened and unopened. Begin with the completed Episode 000 fixture and no Q17/shelf facts. Use real BBS navigation, inspect the index, `SEARCH Q17`, open all required route evidence and `SUBMIT DEFERRED`. Verify the route-specific confirmation/read and exactly one shared proof fact. At the console submit the correct order with proof alone. Expect the training explanation, hidden operation actions and an unchanged save.

Use the actual registry, door host and session to open the Archive, visit the shelf, inspect three fragments, solve the order, read the notebook and EXIT to the main menu. Verify that inspection of fewer than three fragments gives no learned fact. The full route supplies both facts and admits the console application.

As an independent negative case, clone the learned save and remove exactly `deferred-verified`, leaving the learned fact and the already-fired Q17 event. Assert the proof fact is still absent after sign-in, then assert the proof explanation and no write for the same correct command. Start with neither prerequisite and verify the console and Annex are unlisted and direct entry/application has no effect.

**Verification.** Focused Vitest command below. Read the case setup to confirm successful paths never seed either prerequisite.

### 2. Explained failure, durable success and repeat

On an eligible session, submit `APPLY SEAL / ACK / ROUTE` and assert the destination-receipt explanation and a retry or notebook pointer. Check the whole in-memory save, stored bytes and write count, including flags, profile/access source facts, read ledger, events, bulletins, locations and door slot. Check incomplete, duplicate, unknown and extra operation inputs. For the button path, select, clear and re-enter a draft, then observe the same evaluation.

Apply `SEAL / ROUTE / ACK` with the typed command or staged control. Verify the receipt says the working spool is restored and the originals are preserved. Require one write containing the receipt read, event/bulletin and exact `spool-02-restored` flag together. Reload from the serialized bytes with `openSaveSession`, re-enter the console and submit the same answer. Verify the same receipt, no new write/read/bulletin and exactly one restore flag.

**Verification.** Focused Vitest command below. Browser journeys also assert visible feedback and persistence.

### 3. Sector, Annex, MAINTAINER and reactions

Use the real successful saves for the proof/FORGE matrix. Before success, including after a wrong application, assert no SPOOL-02 in `mapNodes` or DIRECTORY / NETWORK, no Annex command or typed entry, and the preexisting access rank and proof-phase dialogue.

After success, SPOOL-02 is available through both map and network projections, the Annex opens from DIRECTORY and displays its recipe plus the three authenticated local fragment records. Rank 2 MAINTAINER is derived from the restore fact and displayed in the BBS menu. Check restored ECHO and SYSOP text supersedes proof commentary, including when both route flags exist. Verify earlier confirmation evidence can still be read. Check PACKET and GHOST annotations through the Annex thread and historical profiles with no TALK affordance.

Verify FORGE tracks its original condition and saved discovery in both branches. Confirm Silent Observatory remains present and unenterable with `NO CARRIER` and `2 OBSERVERS REQUIRED` before and after restoration, and that Episode 000 completion, designation and Observer-related facts are preserved. Assert the door directory exposes only shipped playable doors throughout.

**Verification.** Focused Vitest command below. Existing `journey.spec.ts`, `map.spec.ts`, `forge.spec.ts`, `progress.spec.ts` and BBS browser specs run in the same CI job.

### 4. Production keyboard journey and validated producer

Add a keyboard test in `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` that seeds an eligible version-2 save using `freshSave` and the completed fixture. Carry the designation into the v2 profile, retain Episode 000 completion and add the shared proof and learned facts. Start with no restore flag or receipt. Use Enter, terminal commands and Tab/Shift+Tab plus Enter to open DIRECTORY and the console. Verify the named target and readable prompt, submit a wrong order, then type the correct application, and reach the Annex from DIRECTORY using the keyboard. Check readable Annex recipe, fragment evidence and BBS MAINTAINER status. Reload without reseeding. At the hub, verify STATUS reports MAINTAINER and one Observer online, then sign in and re-enter the Annex.

Add a small pointer case using the same eligible fixture and real order selection, clear and APPLY buttons, then open the Annex. Preserve the existing Q17 and Archive journeys.

In `tests/unit/content.test.ts`, verify the shipped bundle passes validation, the order check owns its endpoint's event-only receipt and its own-read event grants exactly `flag:spool-02-restored`. Remove only the grant in a test copy and expect unknown-producer diagnostics at the Annex/access/sector consumers. Cover unknown prerequisite facts, duplicate or invalid operation definitions, and a wrong/duplicate response publication. Preserve current Q17 validation tests.

**Verification.** Developer runs focused Vitest, `npm run content:validate`, the production build and Playwright collection. CI runs `npm run test:e2e` using the existing workflow.

### Runtime and compatibility coverage

- The unit integration executes in Node 24 on the native Linux Codex workspace. It follows `createBbsDoorSession`, `createBbsProgress`, `settleEvents`, the real door host and save APIs, matching `src/bbs/connection.ts:23` and `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:29`. In a blocked, wrong or repeat submission, assert absence of a new `BbsEffect`. A successful accepted submission takes the same write path as Q17, including the existing handling of save refusal.
- Production browser coverage runs under Chromium on Ubuntu in `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11`. The workflow builds through Playwright global setup, and its fixture serves `dist/` under `/signal-lost/` by request interception. Keep the existing startup checks for failed/off-site requests and errors. In that test, capture startup requests through hub readiness, and assert absence of the BBS connection chunk, content JSON and content manifest requests. Verify by source review that the BBS loads when the player connects and the environment retains its existing import path. The planner/tester sandbox has no browser grant.
- Match `tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts:6` exactly for JavaScript file selection and gzip. The caps remain 60 KiB for `index-` and 170 KiB for `environment-`. Use the approved base values in PLAN.md to assess entry bundle headroom and attach candidate values during development. CI retains its bundle and WebGL checks.

## Developer-owned focused verification

Run with the task's locked Node dependencies and capture command output to role evidence files. The build is required for the gzip measurement, and its `tsc --noEmit` supplies focused static diagnostics for the changed TypeScript. When the workspace is read-only, use a writable copy of the candidate tree and record its identity.

```sh
npm run content:validate
npm test -- tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/unit/access.test.ts tests/unit/world.test.ts tests/unit/voices.test.ts
npx --no-install eslint src/bbs/bbs.ts src/content/schema.ts src/content/validate.ts tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts
npx --no-install prettier --check \
  src/bbs/bbs.ts src/content/schema.ts src/content/validate.ts \
  content/access-levels/maintainer.json content/sectors/spool-02.json \
  content/bbs/deep-field.json content/bbs/spool-02-recovery.json \
  content/bbs/spool-02-restoration-receipt.json content/bbs/maintenance-annex.json \
  content/bbs/maintenance-annex-fragments.json content/bbs/annex-signature-checker.json \

npm run test:e2e -- --list tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts
```

Run this build and gzip check at the first working implementation and for the final candidate if build inputs changed. Record exact gzip bytes and KiB for both files in developer evidence.

```sh
npm run build && node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';

const assets = 'dist/assets';
for (const [prefix, cap] of [['index-', 60], ['environment-', 170]]) {
  const name = readdirSync(assets).find((file) => file.startsWith(prefix) && file.endsWith('.js'));
  if (!name) throw new Error(`Missing bundle: ${prefix}`);
  const bytes = gzipSync(readFileSync(join(assets, name))).length;
  const kib = bytes / 1024;
  console.log(`${name} ${bytes} bytes ${kib.toFixed(4)} KiB (cap ${cap} KiB)`);
  if (kib > cap) process.exitCode = 1;
}
NODE
```

Record the candidate commit or approved base plus working tree checksum, lockfile identity, Node version, command, exit status and output. Include new and modified files in the checksum and match any writable copy to those inputs. Put evidence paths and statuses in the developer handoff. Keep the production build, content validation, focused Vitest, targeted static/format checks and Playwright collection available as separate evidence. Collection demonstrates discovery of the new spec in the existing runner.

## Tester-owned independent review

- Review each acceptance row against the candidate diff and the assertions in its tests. Inspect the two real Q17 producer chains, the Archive's declared reward and the restore event's sole receipt path. Check the case matrix exercises locked, wrong-order, success and replay actions through production entry points with no injected eligibility facts on success. Follow the authored gates through directory and map projections, access rank, BBS dialogue and retained records.
- Inspect the startup import graph and the shipped content changes for out-of-scope paths. Confirm the target card and available operation order give no solution, test data is isolated, and the live console uses current facts. Review the named developer logs, source identity and raw gzip values. Reuse passing results for identical applicable inputs. Repeat only a focused check affected by a relevant change, an observed failure or an unresolved coverage concern. Record independent findings and any new evidence in the tester validation artifact.
- Use the existing Browser tests CI result for browser behavior when it is available for the same candidate. While it is pending, record browser execution as pending and verify spec wiring by source and collection. Agent results are advisory.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy and CI

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base policy from `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml:1` once on the final candidate after roles finish and before publication. It owns claim-bound validation and publication. The policy covers format, lint, build and full unit tests. GitHub Actions runs the existing Browser tests workflow for the PR.

| Command or check | Owner | Expected duration | Evidence, applicability and reuse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Focused checks above, including production build plus Node gzip | developer | Under 5 minutes each on prepared dependencies | Developer evidence files and handoff tied to the candidate input identity. Tester reuses applicable results in its acceptance review. |
| Complete trusted-base required policy, including `npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund && npm test` | coordinator | About 2–5 minutes with the prepared cache, potentially longer on a cold runner. The full unit check has a 15-minute policy timeout. | Claim-bound coordinator validation output for the final candidate and trusted-base policy revision. Publication consumes that result. |
| Browser tests workflow, including install, Chromium provisioning and `npm run test:e2e` | CI | Allow 5–10 minutes for the full workflow including provisioning. The job timeout is 30 minutes. | GitHub Actions **Browser tests / e2e** run for the matching candidate commit, with Playwright failure trace when available. Tester and coordinator reuse the matching run when available. |
